text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali left Rabat for London where he will meet James Baker, the United Nations special envoy in Western Sahara. Baker is also to meet representatives of the Polisario Front, Algeria and Mauritania.
- Istiqlal party leader says participation in June 13 polls is a right, a duty, a responsibility.
- National commission in charge of elections follow-up asks voters to pick up cards and calls for massive turnout.
- U.S. ambassador in Rabat says illiteracy among women is hampering Morocco's economic development and calls for financial reforms to attract foreign investors.
- Morocco considers exporting tomatoes to the United States to get round constraints of European markets.
- Campaigning for local council elections due on June 13 ends today.
